      "observations": [
        "Read full50-line owned diff, exact historical reader/caller and fixed reader/dispatch lifecycle. _findLines replaces one-recursive-call-per-line extraction with an indexed scan across this._buffer. Each CR(13)+LF(10) delimiter pushes the intervening bytes as one string, updates last to after LF and preserves the remaining suffix in one final slice. A trailing CR without LF remains in the suffix for a later read; lone CR or LF is not a delimiter. Empty lines remain possible. These are static control-flow consequences, not executed edge-case tests.",
        "onInputStreamReady appends bytes, frames all available lines, consumes them in order and dispatches either multiline or uppercased command+arguments. Undefined multiline response continues without postCommand/response. Close and STARTTLS paths have separate cleanup; current STARTTLS explicitly clears buffered lines/bytes and returns after switching. Re-arm uses asyncWait and a timeout only while running. No framing change is inferred for outbound response formatting.",
        "The SMTP multiline consumer handles authentication, DATA dot termination and dot unstuffing, then reconstructs stored data using CRLF. Current large-send progress test creates6000 lines and asserts progress/close ordering; that exercises the reader path but does not directly assert chunk-split CRLF, exact framed bytes, memory limits or performance. This patch adds no tests. The previous recursion/multiple slices are gone, but String.fromCharCode.apply still has argument-size and buffering limits; no guarantee for arbitrary line sizes.",
        "Manual style: an indexed for loop is appropriate because delimiter position and slice boundaries are the contract. let last/i replace historical var locals. A short comment explaining retained incomplete suffix would make the boundary easier to see when editing; the for-loop group is clear and no line-per-statement blank-line rule is inferred.
